note: Corpus Corporum's transcription only - Migne's plate is not touched. Verified 2026-08-19 against archive.org patrologiaecurs06saingoog (on disk raw/scans/pl114/), PDF page = (column + 11) / 2, corner numbers checked on every page. Every reading was taken from a full-resolution crop of the whole line at 4-5.5x upscale; nothing was called from a compressed strip.
class: DIGITIZATION CORRUPTION IN BULK - eleven sites in one work. Three sub-kinds: (a) line-break damage, where the plate hyphenates and our source mangles the join (ten atio, viucendum, and the iniquitatibus duplication across a COLUMN break); (b) single-letter substitutions of the OCR kind, which a compositor does not make (acciplunt, Creora, apparel, Filil, aetenam, nis); (c) a lost final letter at an unhyphenated line end (Latin for Latini) and a spurious full stop (filioli.,). WHY IT MATTERS: every one of these had been marked [sic:] or [d:] in the English, i.e. the page was about to assert publicly that MIGNE's plate is defective at eleven places where it is not. The [sic:] marker is a claim about the primary witness and it cannot be made from our files alone.
kept: 0696D 'hae eticorum' is NOT patched: the plate genuinely prints a full word-space where the r belongs, mid-line, with no line break to blame and no broken sort. It is Migne's own defect and its [sic:] stands. That one survivor is why this read was necessary rather than a formality - the OCR-profile hypothesis was right eleven times and wrong once, and only the plate could say which.
